Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — Saturday is a weak, stable day under thick high overcast (100% cloud cover at every site, but with cloud bases far above the thermal tops), so thin sun means soft, low thermals. How fast the air cools with height (lapse rate) is only 5.4 °C/km, well below the 6 °C/km needed for good thermals. Winds are light across the valleys, with northwest flow at Sierra crest height of 21 knots at 8am easing to 10 knots by 4pm. Rainbow Ridge and Hallelujah are the only sites with real thermals; the higher launches are sled rides at best.

Site Breakdown

Rainbow Ridge Favorable — Steady on-launch easterly wind plus the best thermals of the day give a long, usable window.
Window: 11am–3:30pm
Thermal strength is 153–206 ft/min, with the thermal top 959–1,511 ft above ground and peaking around 1pm. Wind is 5–8 mph from 85–101°, right on this east/northeast launch. Ridge lift is +79 to +140 ft/min, below a glider's roughly 200 ft/min sink, so you need the thermals to stay up. This run is a little weaker and later than the last one: peak thermal strength fell from 261 to 210 ft/min and thermal onset moved from 9:30 to 10:30am.

Not recommended today (8) — click a row for details

Kingsbury grade Marginal — Weak, low thermals and near-calm wind that only lines up with the southeast launch in the late morning.
Window: 10am–12pm
Peak thermal strength (w*) is 123–135 ft/min, with the thermal top only 434–705 ft above ground (AGL). That is little more than bumps on the way to a landing zone 2,000 ft below. Wind is 1 mph from about 103° at 10–11am, roughly on launch, then 2–3 mph from the north (behind launch) from noon on. Ridge lift is calm or slightly negative all day.
Hallelujah Marginal — The day's best thermals, but the wind swings to a tailwind from the east-southeast from 2pm.
Window: 11am–1:30pm
Thermal strength climbs from 127 ft/min at 11am to 218 ft/min at 1pm, with the thermal top rising from 655 to about 2,035 ft above ground. Wind is 2–3 mph from 250–286° at 11am–noon, on launch, then 1 mph from 157° at 1pm. From 2pm it turns to 8–13 mph from 103–123°, behind this west/southwest launch. The +68 ft/min of ridge lift at noon is overstated because stable air flows around most of the slope. There is no evening soaring because of that easterly wind.
Slide Mountain Marginal — No thermals at all, so it is sled-only in light southerly wind.
Window: 10am–1pm
Thermal strength is 0 ft/min all day. Wind at launch is 2–5 mph from 170–181°, within the launch range, from 10am to 1pm. It then backs to 200–226° and ridge lift turns to sink of -93 to -166 ft/min from 2pm. Wind 3,000 ft above launch is 23–28 mph from the northwest through noon, so don't expect to climb into calm air. Launch temperature is cold, at 35–42 °F.
Peavine Mountain Marginal — On-launch southerly wind in the afternoon, but thermals are too weak to stay up, so expect a sled ride.
Window: 1pm–3:30pm
Thermal strength peaks at only 73 ft/min at 1pm, with a thermal top of about 450 ft above ground. Wind is 6–9 mph from 183–187° from 1–3pm, well aligned with launch. Ridge lift is near zero (+5 to +8 ft/min), and much of the slope is blocked by stable air. Morning wind is 5–7 mph from about 297°, behind launch, and 3,000 ft above launch it is 23–28 mph from the northwest until noon.
Duck Hill Marginal — Light wind on launch through midday, but ridge lift is too weak to soar and the air is stable.
Window: 8am–1pm
There are essentially no thermals (peak 8 ft/min). Wind is 2–5 mph from 312–11°, on launch, from 8am to 1pm. Ridge lift is +52 to +128 ft/min, but stable air blocks half or more of the slope, so the real lift is less than that. From 2pm the wind is only 1 mph and turns easterly, so there is no evening soaring.
McClellan Unfavorable — Wind stays from the east, outside the south/southwest launch window, and there are almost no thermals.
Peak thermal strength is only 28 ft/min, with a thermal top under 400 ft above ground. Wind is 2–7 mph from 72–96° all day, which is cross to the launch, and ridge lift is negative (-4 to -39 ft/min).
West McClellan Unfavorable — Wind blows from behind the launch all day and there are no usable thermals.
Peak thermal strength is 31 ft/min. Wind is 1–7 mph from 90–139°, a tailwind for this southwest-to-northwest launch, and ridge lift is negative (-45 to -80 ft/min) from 11am.
Daydreams Unfavorable — Near-calm wind, mostly from behind the southwest launch, and no thermals.
Thermal strength is below 40 ft/min all day. Wind is only on launch at 9am (2 mph from 243°), then 1–2 mph and variable to northeasterly for the rest of the day. Ridge lift is calm from 10am, and there is no evening soaring breeze.

Hazards

  • NWS soaring forecast is more pessimistic: The National Weather Service (NWS) Reno soaring forecast has a high of 57 °F, below its 61 °F trigger temperature (the temperature needed for thermals to start). It gives a soaring index of 27 ft/min and a maximum altitude of 5,900 ft above sea level. That points to little or no thermal activity, while this model shows thermals near 200 ft/min at the low sites (Rainbow Ridge, Hallelujah). Treat the thermal forecast with caution.
  • Stronger wind aloft in the morning: Flow at Sierra crest height is from the northwest at 19–21 knots from 8–11am, easing to 10 knots by 4pm. That is below the roughly 25 knots from the west-southwest that usually brings lee-side rotor, so the lee-side risk is unclear rather than high. NWS Reno says Sierra ridge gusts of 40–50 mph will continue this morning before easing. The only ridge-top check (Slide summit, 7am) read 6 mph with gusts to 16 mph against the model's 33 mph. That is one early-run hour, so it is not conclusive.
  • Morning haze: NWS Reno says a temperature inversion may slightly reduce slant visibility around Reno-Tahoe airport until 10am Saturday. Visibility is not in the model.
  • Storm arriving Saturday night and Sunday: NWS Reno expects southwest winds near 10,000 ft of up to 40 knots, with turbulence and low-level wind shear, from late Saturday evening into Sunday morning. This is after sunset and outside Saturday's flying window. Sunday brings strong winds, with Sierra ridge gusts over 95 mph and Lake Wind Advisories from 7am Sunday, then rain and mountain snow from Sunday afternoon.
